summary: Target-level plan for framed deformation groupoids, completed-local comparisons for schemes/spaces and smooth stack presentations, stabilizers, complete-local effectivity and versal algebraization. It imports the already planned A0 approximation/Artin prefix and SF.4 formal geometry, and exports conditional named universal-property adapters for represented parameters. All targets are planned; the explicit geometric supplier and native-interface gaps prevent closed coverage.

nodes.title: Framed deformation groupoids
nodes.statement: For a category fibred in groupoids X over S, an object x₀ over k, and a local Artinian S-algebra A with specified residue identification A/m_A≅k, Def_X,x₀(A) has objects (y,α), y∈X(A), α:x₀≅y|k. An arrow f:(y,α)→(z,β) is an isomorphism over A with (f|k)∘α=β. Base change uses the chosen pullback coherence. The set-valued deformation functor is the set of isomorphism classes of this framed groupoid, not the raw set of objects and not the unframed fibre X(A).
hypotheses: Fix universes and an affine open Spec Λ⊂S containing the image of the point. Use a Noetherian Λ and finite Λ→k with the Artinian coefficient category and its completion imported from SF.4. The classical hull case additionally requires Λ complete local and Λ→k its residue quotient.

For Stacks 98 use k of finite type over S. For a geometric point with a larger residue field use a specified base change to a k-rational point; do not identify its functor with the completion of the original stalk.
proofSteps: Use the native structured-arrow category x₀↓(X(A)→X(k)); arrows in X(k) are invertible.
Restrict its projection to retain the special-fibre identification and pullback constraints. Take the native isomorphism-class quotient only after assembling the groupoid.
Precomposing α by an automorphism of x₀ changes the framing, so this datum is not discarded.
acceptance: Def(k) is contractible even when Aut_X(k)(x₀) is nontrivial.
The residue pullback is not replaced by equality of objects.

sources.match: The special-fibre identification produces a predeformation category and induces the stated maps under morphisms of stacks.

nodes.title: Functoriality of framed comparison
nodes.statement: A morphism X→Y and a chosen identification of its special-fibre object induce Def_X,x₀→Def_Y,y₀. These assignments preserve 2-fibre products: for W=X×_Y Z and w₀=(x₀,z₀,γ₀), Def_W,w₀≃Def_X,x₀×_(Def_Y,y₀)Def_Z,z₀. A representable formally smooth morphism induces a smooth morphism of predeformation categories.
hypotheses: S locally Noetherian; residue k finite type over S; all products are 2-products with their specified gluing isomorphism.
Smoothness means essential surjectivity of the lifting comparison for Artinian surjections; its groupoid definition is imported from SF.4 Part II.
proofSteps: Transport the frame through the morphism using the pullback comparison.
An object of a 2-product consists of two deformations and an isomorphism whose residue is γ₀; the framed constructions match on arrows.
Use representable infinitesimal lifting after forming the fibre product over an Artinian test scheme.
acceptance: The gluing isomorphism survives passage to the framed groupoid.
A strict fibre product of isomorphism-class sets is insufficient when the target has automorphisms.

sources.match: These two comparison properties connect a geometric smooth chart and its relation to the formal deformation category.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal stabilizers
nodes.statement: For a deformation y over A′ and its restriction z over A, Inf(y/z) is the kernel of Aut_A′(y)→Aut_A(z). The infinitesimal stabilizer at x₀ is this kernel for the trivial dual-number deformation over k[ε]→k. Its group law is inherited from automorphisms. It is distinct from the entire residual stabilizer Aut_k(x₀).
hypotheses: Pullback supplies the reduction functor and a specified comparison to z.
The dual-number definition uses the split extension k→k[ε]→k and the trivial pullback of x₀.
proofSteps: Specialize the native kernel of the functor-induced map on automorphism groups.
Conjugating by a special-fibre comparison identifies this kernel with automorphisms of the framed lift.
Import the inertia-stack fibre identification from R09.4; do not construct inertia a second time.
acceptance: For BG_m at its trivial torsor, the dual-number kernel is 1+εk, rather than k×.
For finite constant étale G, Inf(BG)=0 although the residual stabilizer is G.

sources.match: Infinitesimal automorphisms are reduction kernels; their transport depends on the chosen identification.

api.name: InfinitesimalStabilizer.mem_iff
api.statement: Membership means the induced automorphism after reduction is the identity.

api.name: InfinitesimalStabilizer.framedAut

api.name: InfinitesimalStabilizer.faithful

tests.name: StabilizerTests.allKilled

tests.name: StabilizerTests.frameKernel

nodes.title: Linearization and vanishing of stabilizers
nodes.statement: If X satisfies the Rim–Schlessinger condition, Inf_x₀(X) has a natural k-vector-space structure and its addition agrees with composition. For a surjection A′→A of kernel I killed by m_A′ (in particular a small extension), Inf(y/z) is canonically the corresponding additive group Inf_x₀(X)⊗_k I, with identity as its origin. If Inf_x₀(X)=0, every framed Artinian fibre is a setoid and Def_X,x₀ is equivalent to its isomorphism-class functor.
hypotheses: k and the coefficient category follow the framed conventions.
RS is an equivalence of groupoids for the prescribed Artinian ring pullbacks, not merely a surjection on classes.
proofSteps: Apply RS to the automorphism functor at the identity. The two split dual-number directions define addition and scalar multiplication.
Functoriality of composition and its shared identity force vector addition to agree with composition.
Identify the kernel for a surjection annihilated by the maximal ideal with lifts of the identity. Factor arbitrary Artinian surjections into small extensions to propagate vanishing.
acceptance: For BG_m, the infinitesimal group is (k,+) via a↦1+εa.
Finite constant étale BG has no infinitesimal autos but retains its unframed residual autos.

sources.match: RS linearizes reduction kernels and makes the framed category set-valued exactly when infinitesimal autos vanish. Use the untensored tangent-space identification in the proof of 90.19.11, as recorded in source issue E6001; tensor with I once.

nodes.title: Tangent sequence for a 2-fibre product
nodes.statement: For X→Y←Z satisfying RS and a point w₀ of W=X×_Y Z, there is a natural exact sequence of k-vector spaces 0→Inf_W→Inf_X⊕Inf_Z→Inf_Y→T_W→T_X⊕T_Z→T_Y. Here T means isomorphism classes of framed dual-number deformations; the map Inf_Y→T_W changes the gluing isomorphism by an infinitesimal automorphism.
hypotheses: S locally Noetherian; w₀ over a field k finite type over S.
Use the chosen gluing identification at w₀ to compare the Y-valued objects. The two difference maps use compatible opposite signs.
proofSteps: Use framed 2-fibre compatibility.
Construct the boundary by changing the gluing arrow of the trivial dual-number pair. RS makes this construction linear.
An arrow lifts precisely when the corresponding change of gluing can be absorbed into the two source autos; this gives exactness at Inf_Y and T_W. Check the remaining kernels directly.
acceptance: For U→X an atlas and R=U×_X U at the identity arrow, the sequence starts 0→Inf_X→T_R→T_U⊕T_U.
Dropping Inf_Y loses gluing deformations even when X and Z are schemes.

sources.match: The framed 2-product has the six-term tangent and automorphism sequence.
For a chart relation the sequence begins with infinitesimal stabilizers.

nodes.title: Completed local rings of schemes
nodes.statement: For a scheme X and point x, CompletedLocalRing(X,x) is the maximal-ideal adic completion of the actual stalk O_X,x. Its structural map is the native algebra map from the stalk; its n-th jet, indexed from zero, is the projection to O_X,x/m_x^(n+1). Under Noetherianity it is a complete Noetherian local ring with the same residue field. This construction alone says nothing about a stack having a canonical completed local ring.
hypotheses: Noetherianity is required for the stated complete-local properties and for the prorepresentability comparison.
A geometric point with residue extension requires a specified coefficient-compatible model; the original stalk is not relabelled as a k-algebra.
proofSteps: Specialize existing adic completion to the scheme stalk and its native maximal ideal.

Use native quotient evaluations, extensionality, localness, residue-field comparison and maximal-ideal completeness. For Noetherianity use the requested SF.4 commutative-algebra completion theorem: the finitely generated associated graded algebra has finitely generated ideals, whose homogeneous generators lift and generate by completeness.
Retain the quotient indexing convention and structural map when converting to formal deformation maps.
acceptance: The first jet is the residue field, not the quotient by m⁰.
The zero ideal of a field yields the field itself.

sources.match: The completed stalk represents local maps in the deformation comparison.
Ideal-adic completeness and the Noetherianity of completion supply the remaining ring properties.

api.name: CompletedLocalRing.jet_ofStalk

api.name: CompletedLocalRing.isAdicComplete

api.name: CompletedLocalRing.isNoetherianRing

nodes.title: Scheme points and completed local rings
nodes.statement: Let X be locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian S and x a finite-type point with k=κ(x). On C_Λ, the framed deformation functor of X at x is naturally isomorphic to h_R, where R=Ô_X,x and h_R(A) consists of continuous local Λ-algebra maps R→A inducing the specified identity on k. Thus the identity formal family prorepresents this scheme-point deformation functor.
hypotheses: Choose Spec Λ⊂S containing the image of x and the associated residue structure.
For an algebraically closed geometric residue k work with the appropriate k-rational base-changed model. This is a deformation of a point into X, not a deformation of X as a scheme.
proofSteps: A map Spec A→X restricting to x factors through any chosen affine neighbourhood of x and induces a local map O_X,x→A.
Its maximal ideal maps to the nilpotent maximal ideal of A, hence the map factors through some finite jet and extends uniquely to the completion.
The two operations are inverse and compatible with maps in C_Λ. Scheme fibres have no nontrivial arrows, so the groupoid reduces to the represented set-valued functor.
acceptance: At the origin of A¹_k the ring is k[[t]] and a dual-number point sends t to aε.
At the origin of Spec k[u,v]/(uv), the ring is k[[u,v]]/(uv), not the one-parameter smoothing ring of the nodal singularity.

sources.locator: Lemma 98.12.3, proof identification of predeformation categories, pp. 18–19
sources.match: Local maps into a scheme are exactly completion maps on Artinian tests.

nodes.title: Étale charts for space points
nodes.statement: For an algebraic space X locally of finite type over S, a pointed étale chart (U,u)→(X,x) with κ(u)=κ(x)=k induces an equivalence of framed Artinian deformation functors. Consequently Ô_U,u prorepresents the point-deformation functor, and another such chart gives a unique compatible isomorphism of prorepresenting pairs. Do not use an arbitrary smooth chart for this conclusion.
hypotheses: S locally Noetherian and x finite type.
Specify the residue comparison and the chart lift of the point. For a geometric point first pass to the specified residue-field base change.
proofSteps: Étale formal lifting uniquely lifts the nilpotent Artinian test morphism through the chosen residue point.
Compare any two charts through their pointed fibre product, using unique étale lifting.
Apply the scheme completion comparison and uniqueness of the representing natural isomorphism.
acceptance: An étale chart preserves the prorepresenting ring; a positive-dimensional smooth chart adds formal variables.

sources.match: Étale unique lifting gives the pointed functor comparison.
The complete-local space argument uses pointed étale lifts and descent.

nodes.title: Relative dual-number tangent comparison
nodes.statement: For X/S as in the scheme comparison, the tangent space of its framed point functor is Der_Λ(O_X,x,k) at the specified residue point. For a k-rational point of a k-scheme this is naturally Hom_k(m_x/m_x²,k), hence the existing ZariskiTangentSpace(X,x). For a general relative base retain relative differentials or derivations; the absolute stalk cotangent dual is not asserted to equal the relative tangent.
hypotheses: The k-rational special case fixes base S=Spec k and its structural k-algebra map.
For an arbitrary point map use the algebra structure it induces on k in a fresh local scope, as required by the native dual-number equivalence.
proofSteps: Restrict the natural comparison to k[ε].
Apply the pinned dual-number lift–derivation equivalence with the correct algebra tower.

The affine rational-point cotangent localization equivalence is already pinned Tau Ceti. Dualize that equivalence and use the usual derivation–cotangent universal property imported from SF.1; reduce a non-affine point to its affine neighbourhood. Only the geometric functor transport is new.
acceptance: The tangent to A¹_k at zero has dimension one.
The tangent to a point over itself is zero, including when its absolute residue-field derivations over a smaller field are nonzero.

sources.match: Scheme tangent vectors are coefficient-relative dual-number lifts.
The represented tangent is the derivation module at the chosen residue map.

nodes.title: Coherent formal objects
nodes.statement: For a fixed complete Noetherian local S-algebra R with residue k, a formal object of X is a tower ξ_n∈X(R/m_R^(n+1)), n≥0, with restriction isomorphisms ξ_(n+1)|_(R/m^(n+1))≅ξ_n. Morphisms are levelwise arrows commuting with these comparisons. Composites of adjacent comparisons define all longer transitions. The category is a groupoid at fixed R, and changes of complete local base use coherent pullback.
hypotheses: Use positive quotient powers indexed from zero and the actual restriction functors.
In the Stacks convention k is finite type over S. The generic native prototype accepts a specified tower of groupoids; assembling X(R/m^(n+1)) is an explicit D0 supplier contract.
proofSteps: Construct objects with isomorphism gluing rather than equalities of chosen fibre objects.
Define arrows, identities, composition and inverses componentwise; the commutation law makes them well-defined.
Use the chosen base restriction coherence to obtain the full completion category. For setoid fibres this agrees with the existing A0 compatible-point limit.
acceptance: Compatible objects do not suffice without compatible arrows.
Taking isomorphism classes term by term can lose the chosen transition data.

sources.match: Formal objects retain transition maps and commuting morphisms.
Groupoid-valued completion is a coherent tower rather than a set of classes.

api.name: FormalObject.evaluation
api.statement: The n-th object/arrow evaluation is a functor to X(R/m^(n+1)).

api.name: FormalObject.hom_ext
api.statement: Two formal arrows are equal if all their levelwise arrows agree.

api.name: FormalObject.isomorphism_iff
api.statement: An isomorphism of formal objects is equivalent to a family of levelwise isomorphisms commuting with gluing.

tests.name: FormalTests.point
tests.statement: The constant discrete point tower has one object up to isomorphism.

tests.name: FormalTests.compatibleArrows
tests.statement: Every formal arrow must commute with each gluing square; an incompatible component sequence is excluded.

tests.name: FormalTests.automorphisms
tests.statement: For a constant one-object groupoid tower with identity reduction, evaluation at level zero identifies formal automorphisms with the group at that level, even when gluing is nontrivial.

uses.how: State effectivity as an equivalence/essential image of the full formal groupoid.
Compare the universal object at every quotient, including its automorphisms.

nodes.title: Effectivity of formal objects
nodes.statement: Let res_R:X(R)→FormalObject_X(R) be the coherent restriction functor. A formal object ξ is effective if there is y∈X(R) with a specified isomorphism res_R(y)≅ξ. Effectivity of all objects is essential surjectivity. Full faithfulness of res_R is a separate property required to compare arrows and descend algebraizations; equivalence combines both properties.
hypotheses: R complete Noetherian local over S with the fixed residue convention.
The affine set-valued A0 effectivity predicate is imported only after passing to setoid fibres; it does not imply groupoid equivalence.
proofSteps: Construct res_R from actual pullback and its coherence.
Use its native essential image for object effectivity, retaining the comparison isomorphism.
Use native fully faithful/essentially surjective vocabulary for morphism effectivity and equivalence.
acceptance: An algebraization with a specified formal comparison is unique up to unique comparison-compatible isomorphism only under full faithfulness.

sources.match: The object condition is essential image, while the subsequent stack theorem asserts a full equivalence.

api.name: IsEffective.ofRestriction
api.statement: Every object actually restricted from X(R) is effective.

api.name: IsEffective.iso_iff
api.statement: An isomorphism of formal objects transports effectivity.

api.name: IsEffective.all_iff
api.statement: All formal objects are effective iff res_R is essentially surjective.

tests.name: EffectiveTests.identity
tests.statement: Identity restriction makes every object effective.

tests.name: EffectiveTests.empty
tests.statement: A functor from the empty groupoid cannot effect any object of a nonempty formal target.

tests.name: EffectiveTests.notFullyFaithful
tests.statement: The constant functor from the one-object groupoid of (ℤ,+) to the formal point tower is essentially surjective and is not faithful. Object effectivity must not imply equivalence.

uses.how: Supply the effective complete-local object before invoking approximation.
Keep the criterion’s effectivity input separate from its conclusion of algebraicity.

nodes.title: Restriction from complete rings to spaces
nodes.statement: For any algebraic space X over S and a complete Noetherian local S-algebra R, restriction gives a bijection Mor_S(Spec R,X)→lim_(n≥0) Mor_S(Spec(R/m^(n+1)),X). No properness, separatedness or finite-presentation condition on X is required for this statement.
hypotheses: R is complete, separated, local and Noetherian.
This theorem concerns maps from the fixed complete local base, not existence of a finite-type algebraization of an arbitrary formal scheme.
proofSteps: For schemes every map from the local test rings lies in a single affine neighbourhood; compatible ring maps have a unique complete limit.
For space injectivity, the equalizer is a locally quasi-finite separated scheme; all-order agreement forces equality at its local ring.

For surjectivity choose a pointed étale cover after a finite separable residue extension, lift to its finite étale complete-local extension, effect the scheme maps, then descend using injectivity on the finite product of complete local overlap rings.
acceptance: Both existence and uniqueness of the compatible map are proved.
The formal-space map out of Spf R is not silently identified with an arbitrary scheme-valued formal family.

sources.match: Maps out of a complete local ring into an algebraic space are determined and effected by their formal restrictions.

nodes.title: Effectivity for algebraic stacks
nodes.statement: Let S be locally Noetherian and X an algebraic stack over S. Restriction from objects over complete Noetherian local S-algebras with residue field finite type over S to formal objects is an equivalence, compatible with change of such bases. In particular each res_R is fully faithful and essentially surjective.
hypotheses: Algebraicity of X is already established; this result cannot supply the effectivity hypothesis while algebraicity is still being proved.
The diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces and an actual smooth surjective atlas exists.
proofSteps: For full faithfulness represent Isom(y,z) by an algebraic space and apply complete-local space restriction.

For objects choose a smooth atlas, pass to a finite separable residue extension and its finite étale complete local ring, and recursively lift a compatible atlas point across successive square-zero quotients.
Effect the scheme map; full faithfulness identifies descent arrows over the overlap and proves their cocycle. Effective fppf descent gives the object over R and its specified all-order comparison.
acceptance: BG_m keeps the automorphisms of the algebraized torsor.
Grothendieck existence for coherent sheaves is not needed in this direct chart-and-descent proof.

sources.match: The equivalence is proved using space-valued Isom and smooth-atlas descent.

nodes.title: Effectivity and 2-fibre products
nodes.statement: If complete-local restriction is an equivalence for X, Y and Z, it is an equivalence for X×_Y Z. Compatible objects and the comparison isomorphism are all algebraized; uniqueness of the isomorphism follows from full faithfulness for Y.
hypotheses: The three categories are fibred in groupoids over S; equivalences are compatible with base change.
All three equivalences are hypotheses; mere object effectivity in Y is insufficient.
proofSteps: Identify restriction for the product as the 2-product of the three restriction functors.
Effect the two objects, lift the gluing isomorphism through the Y equivalence, and transport the coherence.
Use equivalence invariance of 2-products for arrows and base maps.
acceptance: A formal Isom arrow between two effective objects is effected, rather than replaced by an equality of their classes.

sources.match: The complete-local restriction equivalence is stable under 2-fibre products.

nodes.title: Versality of algebraic families
nodes.statement: Let U be locally of finite type over S, y∈X(U), u a finite-type point and x₀=y|κ(u). The family is versal at u if the induced map Def_U,u→Def_X,x₀ is smooth: for each Artinian surjection B→A the comparison Def_U,u(B)→Def_U,u(A)×_(Def_X,x₀(A))Def_X,x₀(B) is essentially surjective. The 2-product retains its comparison arrow. A formal object ξ over R is versal if h_R→Def_X,x₀ has the same lifting property.
hypotheses: S locally Noetherian, X fibred in groupoids, k=κ(u) finite type over S.
Use the groupoid version of SF.4 smoothness, not an unframed surjectivity statement on objects.
proofSteps: Use the family and 2-Yoneda to assemble its pointed morphism of deformation categories.
Form the actual lifting 2-product at each Artinian surjection.
Factor any Artinian surjection into small extensions, so testing those suffices; this is the imported formal-deformation lifting theorem.
acceptance: Versality does not require tangent bijectivity.
The lift includes an isomorphism compatible with the specified A-deformation.

sources.match: Pointed smoothness defines versality; completion preserves it and RS gives its finite residue-extension compatibility.

sources.locator: Definition 90.8.1, Lemma 90.8.2 and Remark 90.8.3, pp. 20–21; Situation 90.29.1 and Lemma 90.29.5, pp. 71–73
sources.match: Lifting uses the comparison 2-product; small extensions suffice, and finite residue extension preserves smoothness.

api.name: FamilyVersalAt.smallExtension_iff
api.statement: It suffices to test small extensions: surjections with nonzero principal kernel killed by the source maximal ideal. Equivalently one may test all surjections with kernel killed by that ideal.

api.name: FamilyVersalAt.completion_iff
api.statement: The family is versal at u iff its completed-local formal object is versal.

api.name: FamilyVersalAt.finiteResidueExtension
api.statement: Under RS, finite residue extensions preserve the smooth pointed deformation morphism.

tests.name: VersalTests.identity
tests.statement: The identity family of a locally finite-type scheme is versal at every finite-type point.

tests.name: VersalTests.excessParameter
tests.statement: A¹_k→Spec k is smooth and versal at zero; its tangent map k→0 is not bijective, so it is not a hull.

tests.name: VersalTests.closedPoint
tests.statement: Spec k→A¹_k at zero is not versal: the dual-number point t↦ε cannot lift through the closed point.

uses.how: Upgrade the approximated effective object to an all-orders algebraization.
Recognize completed smooth charts and distinguish miniversal families from arbitrary charts.

nodes.title: Versality and completed local rings
nodes.statement: For y over U locally of finite type over locally Noetherian S and a finite-type u, let ξ be its formal restriction over R=Ô_U,u. Then y is versal at u iff ξ is versal. For a morphism U→V of schemes locally of finite type over S, this is also equivalent to the morphism being smooth at u.
hypotheses: Use the same coefficient and residue maps for h_R and Def_U,u.
The scheme smoothness conclusion applies to a genuine locally finite-type scheme morphism; no arbitrary CFG is declared smooth from a predicate alone.
proofSteps: Identify Def_U,u with h_R by the completed-local universal property.
The morphism induced by y under this identification is exactly the morphism of its formal object.
For schemes apply the local infinitesimal criterion of smoothness with the stated finiteness assumptions.
acceptance: The same chart and residue point occur in both versality predicates.

sources.match: Completion preserves the precise lifting condition; the scheme case recovers smoothness.

nodes.title: Smooth charts and hull comparisons
nodes.statement: A smooth representable chart U→X at a specified lift u of x₀ induces a smooth h_(Ô_U,u)→Def_X,x₀, hence a versal formal family. In the classical equal-residue coefficient setting, its isomorphism-class transformation is a hull exactly when its tangent map is bijective. Under RS and Inf_X,x₀=0 the framed category is setoid-valued; if the chart map is also tangent-bijective, the SF.4 prorepresentability criterion makes this pair prorepresent the framed functor. Inf=0 alone does not make an arbitrary smooth-chart ring prorepresent it.
hypotheses: S locally Noetherian; U locally finite type over S; u finite type with the fixed residue field.

For the hull/prorepresentability clause use coefficient residue k and the classical SF.4 H1–H4 conditions. Exclude the inseparable-residue orbit notion of minimality from the tangent-bijective clause.
proofSteps: Representable smooth lifting makes the pointed chart morphism smooth; use the completion identification.
The definition of hull adds tangent bijectivity to this smooth transformation.
When Inf=0, RS passes through the setoid equivalence to give the required set-valued gluing. Apply the imported prorepresentability criterion and its smooth tangent-bijective comparison theorem.
acceptance: The smooth chart A¹→point gives k[[t]] although the point is prorepresented by k.
For finite étale BG with algebraically closed k the framed functor is terminal and prorepresented by k, while BG is still not a fine unframed space.

sources.match: A smooth chart and its completion are versal.
Vanishing infinitesimal autos gives a setoid functor; tangent bijectivity is separately needed for the hull comparison.

nodes.title: Completed presentations of deformation groupoids
nodes.statement: For a smooth pointed atlas U→X of an algebraic stack, the framed deformation category at x₀ is equivalent to the groupoid quotient of Def_U,u by Def_(U×_X U),r, where r is the identity relation point (u,u,id). The object functor is represented by Ô_U,u; the relation functor is represented through a pointed étale chart of the algebraic space U×_X U at r. Source, target, identity, inverse and composition are the induced formal maps, and their coherence is retained. This is a presentation, not a choice-independent ring attached to X.
hypotheses: Residue points u,r have the fixed k; use the geometric base change when needed.
U is locally finite type over S locally Noetherian. X satisfies RS, as algebraic stacks do.

The relation chart is étale with the prescribed residue field; its completion represents the identity-framed relation functor. The unframed stabilizer has other residual arrows that are not included in this single formal neighbourhood.
proofSteps: Apply framed 2-fibre compatibility to U×_X U at the identity arrow.
Smooth lifting of the atlas makes Def_U,u essentially surjective onto the framed category on Artinian tests.
The relation arrows and composition recover that category by the imported groupoid-quotient presentation theorem; replace the scheme/space point functors by their completion representatives.
acceptance: For BG_m, the object functor of a pointed atlas can be terminal while the identity formal relation has 1+εk automorphisms.
For a scheme chart of the identity, the relation introduces no additional stabilizers.

sources.match: Framed deformation preserves the atlas relation 2-fibre product.
A smooth deformation presentation recovers the category and its stabilizer kernel.

nodes.title: Algebraization of effective versal formal objects
nodes.statement: Let S be locally Noetherian, X fibred in groupoids and limit preserving on objects, and ξ a formal object over a complete Noetherian local S-algebra R with residue k finite type over S, image s∈S. If ξ is effective and versal and O_S,s is a G-ring, there are U→S of finite type, a finite-type u∈U with κ(u)=k, and y∈X(U), versal at u, with an isomorphism R≅Ô_U,u and a compatible identification of all the ξ_n with the formal restrictions of y. The isomorphism and family need not be unique.
hypotheses: All four inputs—effectivity, versality, local G-ring and limit preservation on objects—are supplied before applying the theorem.
No representable-diagonal or Artin-algebraicity conclusion is used in this theorem.
The completion isomorphism is existential. It is not a promise to algebraize a prescribed arbitrary formal coordinate change exactly.
proofSteps: Effect ξ by an object over Spec R. Apply the imported A0 approximation theorem at N=2, preserving the second jet and associated graded dimensions.

Versality recursively lifts the approximation to all orders and gives a compatible local map R→Ô_U,u. The second-jet agreement makes this map surjective by the complete-local Nakayama criterion imported from SF.4.
Associated graded dimension equality gives equal finite lengths at every quotient, making the surjections isomorphisms. Pass to the complete limit and transfer versality back to the algebraic family.
acceptance: Approximation of a nonversal formal object provides only finite-jet agreement; it does not prove this all-order conclusion.
Dropping the G-ring input is excluded by the source’s counterexample in 98.12.8.

sources.match: Versality upgrades the imported finite-jet approximation of an effective object to the completed-local isomorphism.

nodes.title: Formal universal properties of represented parameters
nodes.statement: Over a locally Noetherian S, given a locally finite-type parameter scheme P→S and a parameter functor F on S-schemes with a supplied natural representation θ:Hom_S(-,P)≅F and a finite-type p∈P, let ξ₀=θ(p). Transport schemeFramedCompletionEquiv through θ to obtain h_(Ô_P,p)≅Def_F,ξ₀. Export the representation, universal object, pullback naturality and this formal comparison under named projective-bundle, Grassmannian, flag, Hilbert, Quot, Hom, Isom and Picard-space interfaces. Space-valued parameters use the pointed étale chart comparison instead. Their original representability and geometric hypotheses remain with R09.1/R09.2/SF.1; this node proves only the uniform point/completion transport.
hypotheses: For the scheme completion use P locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian S and p a finite-type point. For the space version use such a pointed étale chart with the same residue field; a chart with a residue extension is a different coefficient problem.
For projective/Grassmann/flag use the supplier quotient convention: locally free quotients, flags of quotients with compatible kernels.

For Hilbert/Quot use the exact base, projectivity, finite-presentation, sheaf and polynomial conditions from the representing theorem. Hom/Isom require their own representability hypotheses; they are not asserted representable for arbitrary schemes.
Fix the functor’s base-change and isomorphism-class conventions. Universal quotient/family flatness is over P and does not assert P→S flat.
proofSteps: Take the universal element θ_P(id_P) and evaluate the supplied natural isomorphism on each test scheme.
Naturality identifies arbitrary classified objects with pullbacks of this universal element, including Artinian residue framing.

Transport the completed-local natural isomorphism and record one named interface per parameter kind. Supplier base-change identifications transport the finite Artinian comparisons; do not assert arbitrary-base-change commutation of stalk completion without hypotheses.
acceptance: Every parameter consumed by the arithmetic roadmap has a named representation and completed-local comparison with its universal object.
The adapter never substitutes a coarse space for the groupoid of a stack with stabilizers.

sources.match: The representing-point deformation comparison transports along an already supplied natural representation.

api.name: ParameterFormalExports.classify
api.statement: For a supplied θ and test T, its component gives Hom_S(T,P)≃F(T).

api.name: ParameterFormalExports.universal
api.statement: The universal element is the image of id_P.

api.name: ParameterFormalExports.classify_natural
api.statement: Classifying f∘g agrees with pullback of classify(f) along g.

api.name: projectiveParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: A quotient line of E at p has the deformation functor represented by Ô_(P(E)),p, under the supplier quotient convention.

api.name: grassmannParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: Rank-r locally free quotient deformations are represented by the completed stalk of the supplied Grassmannian.

api.name: flagParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: Compatible quotient flags at p have the completed-stalk formal universal property of the supplied flag scheme.

api.name: hilbertParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: Deformations of the specified flat closed subscheme with fixed Hilbert polynomial are classified by the supplied Hilbert completion, with universal family pulled back.

api.name: quotParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: Deformations of the specified flat quotient of E, modulo compatible quotient isomorphism, are classified by the supplied Quot completion.

api.name: homParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: Deformations of a specified morphism in the supplied representable Hom functor are classified by its completed parameter stalk.

api.name: isomParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: Deformations of a specified isomorphism are classified by the supplied Isom completion and retain the invertibility requirement.

api.name: picardParameter_formalEquiv
api.statement: The framed deformation of a class in the supplied relative Picard sheaf is represented by a pointed étale-chart completion of its Picard space; this does not classify arrows of the Picard stack.

tests.name: ParameterTests.identityRepresentation
tests.statement: For F=Hom(-,P) and θ=id, classify is the identity on actual arrows.

tests.name: ParameterTests.universalElement
tests.statement: The universal element classifies id_P, rather than a selected unrelated object.

tests.name: ParameterTests.pullback
tests.statement: Classifying a composition agrees with applying the contravariant functor map to the class of the outer arrow.

tests.name: ParameterTests.grassmannEndpoints
tests.statement: For E of rank n, rank-zero and rank-n quotient functors are terminal over S; over a rational field-base point their framed tangent is zero.

tests.name: ParameterTests.hilbertNonflatBase
tests.statement: For S=Spec k[ε] and X=Spec k closed in S, the degree-one Hilbert parameter is X. Its universal family over itself is flat although X→S is not flat; only Artinian S-maps satisfying ε=0 are classified.

tests.name: ParameterTests.quotLengthOne
tests.statement: For E=O on P¹_k, a length-one quotient at a rational origin has point-deformation completion k[[t]], since it is the length-one Hilbert functor of P¹.

tests.name: ParameterTests.isomUnit
tests.statement: For endomorphisms of the trivial line over A, Hom gives A and Isom gives A×; an Artinian endomorphism reducing to 1 is invertible, while zero is excluded.

tests.name: ParameterTests.picardAutomorphisms
tests.statement: For X=Spec A over itself the relative Picard sheaf is terminal, while its line-bundle groupoid has the units A× as automorphisms of the trivial object. The Picard-space completion must not be substituted for the Picard-stack groupoid.

uses.how: Consume named parameter universal properties while the application proves its own deformation/obstruction conditions.
Use completed classifying rings and preserve the chosen universal objects.

nodes.title: Transfer to arithmetic moduli
nodes.statement: Given a supplied algebraic moduli stack M of the required elliptic/abelian objects, an equivalence between its framed fibre and the arithmetic deformation groupoid transports the completed-atlas presentation, infinitesimal stabilizers, tangent comparison and complete-local effectivity to that problem. If the formal object is effective and versal, the G-ring and limit-preservation inputs give a finite-type versal family via effectiveVersal_algebraization. A rigidifying level yields a represented local functor only after the supplied level theorem removes the required automorphisms. Coarse moduli alone does not supply this equivalence.
hypotheses: The arithmetic definition, deformation theory and algebraicity are application inputs from the corresponding R10/R13 owners; no abelian or elliptic deformation theorem is reconstructed here.

For an Artin proof use the imported A0 criterion with the complete hypothesis ledger recorded in targetMatrix; effectivity must be independently proved, for example by the imported SF.4 formal-existence theorem in its exact proper/projective setting.
For coherent families on an already fixed proper scheme use SF.4 Grothendieck existence; arbitrary varying formal schemes need a separate effectivity/algebraization theorem.
proofSteps: Pull each general comparison through the supplied equivalence of framed groupoids, including arrows and universal objects.
For already algebraic M apply complete-local restriction; for a candidate CFG use its separate effectivity supplier before invoking A0 Artin.
Apply the effective-versal theorem with all hypotheses checked. Use only the precise automorphism-rigidity and parameter interfaces supplied for the chosen level.
acceptance: For E₀ over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, import ModularCurves 7D’s marked universal deformation over W(k)[[T]] and 7B’s completed strict-henselian local-moduli comparison for a rigidified representing scheme. Transport the universal family and rigidifier through the supplied framed equivalence; do not infer this comparison for an unrigidified coarse space.
Finite residual inertia with Inf=0 is insufficient to assert an unframed fine moduli scheme.
Proper coherent Grothendieck existence is not an assertion that every formal deformation of every higher-dimensional scheme is algebraizable.

sources.locator: Lemma 98.9.5, pp. 12–14; Lemma 98.12.7, pp. 20–21; Proposition 98.16.1 and Lemma 98.17.1, pp. 26–27
sources.match: The general comparison is reusable by arithmetic moduli once their own object, effectivity and rigidity hypotheses are supplied.

requests.need: Supply the existing ordinary Cat-valued stack/CFG interfaces specialized to schemes over S: fibre groupoids, coherent pullback, 2-products, 2-Yoneda and fppf descent. Connect the native framed structured-arrow and fixed-ring tower prototypes to those fibres. This requests the relative adapters, not a replacement for existing native pseudofunctor/stack machinery.

Supply algebraic-space schemes of Isom and pointed étale charts with chosen residue-field identifications; unique lifting across nilpotent thickenings, smooth lifting, finite étale complete-local extensions of separable residue extensions, and local differential/cotangent comparisons. Space restriction needs fppf sheaf descent and equalizer local-ring arguments. These are exact space extensions of the scheme substrate.

Part II: extend its set-valued deformation/hull interfaces to coherent groupoid-valued completion, smooth lifting by essential surjectivity, RS vector-space structures and 2-fibre tangent exactness, plus complete-local Nakayama and quotient presentation coherence. Export its existing proper coherent Grothendieck existence and effective formal curve-deformation theorems with comparison-compatible arrows. Preserve classical equal-residue hull hypotheses versus inseparable minimality. Supply Noetherianity of ideal-adic completion under Noetherianity of the original ring (Stacks 10.97.5–6, pp. 227–228); native Mathlib already supplies maximal-ideal completeness, localness and residue-field comparison.

Supply projective, Grassmannian and flag quotient-classifying natural isomorphisms and universal quotient objects, coherent base change and chosen-point transport. R09.6 adds only their uniform completed-local adapters; AlgebraicVectorBundles current main explicitly assigns these constructions to a separate roadmap.

Supply each Hilbert, Quot, Hom and Isom representing natural isomorphism under the exact theorem hypotheses, universal families/quotients and base change. Keep flatness of universal families separate from flatness of the parameter over S. Hom and Isom have their own finiteness/properness conditions.

Supply the actual established algebraic-stack presentations used here, including representable algebraic-space diagonals and smooth atlases; verify RS for them. Inertia itself is already imported by its named node. Do not infer stack algebraicity from this packet’s conditional comparison.

Supply the specific auxiliary-level automorphism-removal theorem and its base/characteristic/level hypotheses, and its comparison to the fine moduli problem. A coarse space or zero infinitesimal stabilizer alone does not remove residual automorphisms.

Import G-rings, regular local completion maps and Popescu at their accepted sole owner. A0’s approximation prefix consumes them before its Artin criteria; R09.6 consumes that prefix. No reverse R09.6→A0 edge is proposed.

Import the existing completed strict-henselian local-ring comparison for a geometric point of a rigidified finite moduli scheme, including the universal family, level and change-of-rigidifier compatibility.

Import the existing marked elliptic deformation groupoid and universal family over W(k)[[T]] for k algebraically closed of characteristic p. R09.6 supplies only transfer along the given framed equivalence.

The eight named geometric formal adapters and their concrete tests must be instantiated against those carriers. Arithmetic consumers supply their own groupoid equivalence, effectivity, Artin hypothesis checks and level rigidity; this packet proves conditional transfer, not those application-specific claims.
